ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontally placed rectangle ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; AB is the vertical side, and BC is the bottom side. Another tilted rectangle AECF shares the points A and C in the diagonal direction with the horizontal rectangle, point F is above the horizontal rectangle, and point E is below the horizontal rectangle. The gray shaded part is the overlapping region inside the two rectangles, located within the horizontal rectangle ABCD, and the two small right triangles on the left and right are cut off by the two slanted sides AE and FC of the tilted rectangle. Reasoning: Set coordinates according to the figure as A=(0,3), B=(0,0), C=(11,0), D=(11,3), then the area of the horizontal rectangle ABCD is 3×11=33. Let d=C-A=(11,-3), and let p=AF. Because AECF is a rectangle, AF is perpendicular to FC, and FC=d-p. It is known that |AF|=7, |FC|=9, so p·(d-p)=0, that is, p·d=|p|^2=49. Combining with F being above in the figure, obtain p=(364/65,273/65), therefore FC=d-p=(351/65,-468/65). So the magnitude of the slope of FC is (468/65)/(351/65)=468/351=4/3; AE, which is parallel to it, also has the same slope magnitude. The height of the horizontal rectangle is 3, therefore the corresponding horizontal distance when each slanted side passes through height 3 is 3/(4/3)=9/4. Thus the two unshaded regions on the left and right inside ABCD are two congruent right triangles, each with area (1/2)×3×(9/4)=27/8. The shaded area is 33-2×27/8=33-27/4=105/4. Therefore m=105, n=4, m+n=109.

The height of the horizontal rectangle is 3, therefore the corresponding horizontal distance when each slanted side passes through height 3 is 3/(4/3)=9/4.
